body.en: Linear equations, systems, and inequalities constitute the single largest tested domain on the EST I Mathematics exam (roughly 35% of all questions). Mastery requires algebraic speed, geometric interpretation of slopes and intercepts, determining system consistency (unique, no solution, or infinitely many solutions), and modeling real-world constraints.

label.en: Definition 1.1 — Linear Forms, Slope, and Parallel/Perpendicular Criteria

body.en:
Essential forms of linear equations and geometric properties:
  • Slope-Intercept Form: \(y = mx + b\), where \(m\) is the constant rate of change (slope) and \(b\) is the \(y\)-intercept \((0, b)\).
    \[ m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1} = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} \]
  • Point-Slope Form: \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\), ideal for writing the equation of a line given slope \(m\) and any point \((x_1, y_1)\).
  • Standard Form: \(Ax + By = C\), where \(A, B, C\) are integers. The slope is \(m = -\frac{A}{B}\), the \(x\)-intercept is \(\left(\frac{C}{A}, 0\right)\), and the \(y\)-intercept is \(\left(0, \frac{C}{B}\right)\).
  • Parallel and Perpendicular Lines:
    Parallel lines share identical slopes: \(m_1 = m_2\) and \(b_1 \neq b_2\).
    Perpendicular lines have negative reciprocal slopes: \(m_1 \cdot m_2 = -1 \iff m_2 = -\frac{1}{m_1}\) (for non-vertical lines).

label.en: ● Deep Conceptual Intuition — Heart of Algebra

body.en: Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST I — Literacy & Math), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

label.en: Theorem 1.1 — System Consistency and Absolute Value Inequalities

body.en:
Analytical criteria for systems of equations and compound inequalities:
  • Classification of Linear Systems: For a \(2 \times 2\) system:
    \[ \begin{cases} a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1 \\ a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2 \end{cases} \]
    1. Unique Solution: \(\frac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \frac{b_1}{b_2}\) (lines intersect at a single point).
    2. No Solution (Inconsistent): \(\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \frac{c_1}{c_2}\) (parallel lines, identical slopes, distinct intercepts).
    3. Infinitely Many Solutions (Dependent): \(\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{c_1}{c_2}\) (coincident lines).
  • Absolute Value Inequalities (for \(c > 0\)):
    1. Less than (Conjunction / "And"):
    \[ |ax + b| < c \iff -c < ax + b < c \]
    2. Greater than (Disjunction / "Or"):
    \[ |ax + b| > c \iff ax + b > c \quad \text{or} \quad ax + b < -c \]
  • Inequality Multiplication Rule: Multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative real number strictly reverses the inequality symbol:
    \[ -kx \le c \iff x \ge -\frac{c}{k} \quad (k > 0) \]

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Linear Equations & Systems

body.en:
• Inequality Sign Flip: When multiplying or dividing both sides of an inequality by a negative number, you MUST reverse the inequality symbol: \(-3x < 12 \implies x > -4\).
  • Infinite vs. No Solution: If solving leads to a true identity like \(0 = 0\), the system has infinitely many solutions (coincident lines). If it leads to a contradiction like \(0 = 7\), there is no solution (parallel lines).
  • Slope from Standard Form: For \(Ax + By = C\), the slope is \(m = -A/B\) and the \(y\)-intercept is \(C/B\). Do not forget the negative sign on \(A/B\)!
  • Absolute Value with Variable on Both Sides: In equations like \(|2x - 5| = 3x - 1\), you must check both tentative solutions in the original equation to reject extraneous roots where \(3x - 1 < 0\).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Heart of Algebra)

body.en:
Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

label.en: Worked Example 1.A — Multi-Step Linear Equation with Grouping

body.en:
Solve the equation \(3(2x - 5) - 4(x + 2) = 11\) for \(x\).

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Apply the distributive property to expand both grouped terms:
    \[ 6x - 15 - 4x - 8 = 11 \]
  2. Combine like terms on the left side:
    \[ (6x - 4x) + (-15 - 8) = 11 \implies 2x - 23 = 11 \]
  3. Add 23 to both sides to isolate the variable term:
    \[ 2x = 11 + 23 \implies 2x = 34 \]
  4. Divide by 2:
    \[ x = \frac{34}{2} = \mathbf{17} \]
The solution is \(\mathbf{x = 17}\).

label.en: Worked Example 1.B — System with Infinitely Many Solutions

body.en:
For what value of the constant \(k\) does the following system have infinitely many solutions?
\[ \begin{cases} kx - 6y = 10 \\ 4x - 3y = 5 \end{cases} \]
Step-by-step Solution:
  1. A linear system has infinitely many solutions when the two equations represent the exact same line, meaning all corresponding coefficient ratios are equal:
    \[ \frac{k}{4} = \frac{-6}{-3} = \frac{10}{5} \]
  2. Calculate the constant scaling ratio:
    \[ \frac{-6}{-3} = 2, \qquad \frac{10}{5} = 2 \]
  3. Set the \(x\)-coefficient ratio equal to 2:
    \[ \frac{k}{4} = 2 \implies k = 4 \times 2 = \mathbf{8} \]
When \(k = \mathbf{8}\), the first equation is exactly twice the second equation, producing infinitely many solutions.

label.en: Worked Example 1.C — Absolute Value Compound Inequality

body.en:
Solve the inequality \(|3x - 4| \le 11\) and write the solution in interval notation.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Rewrite the absolute value inequality as a three-part compound inequality:
    \[ -11 \le 3x - 4 \le 11 \]
  2. Add 4 to all three parts:
    \[ -11 + 4 \le 3x \le 11 + 4 \implies -7 \le 3x \le 15 \]
  3. Divide all parts by 3 (since 3 is positive, inequality directions remain unchanged):
    \[ -\frac{7}{3} \le x \le 5 \]
In interval notation, the solution is \(\mathbf{\left[-\frac{7}{3}, 5\right]}\).

label.en: Worked Example \(D\) — Heart of Algebra (Medium Application)

body.en:
Problem (Medium): A particle's position in the xy-plane at time \(t\) is given by the parametric equations \(x(t) = t^2 - 6t\) and \(y(t) = t^3 - 9t\), where \(t \geq 0\). The particle starts at the origin and moves along a path. Find the time \(t > 0\) when the particle returns to the x-axis, and determine the x-coordinate of this position.

Step-by-Step Solution: The particle returns to the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0. We are given \(y(t) = t^3 - 9t\). Setting \(y(t) = 0\) and factoring, we get: \[ t^3 - 9t = 0 \] \[ t(t^2 - 9) = 0 \] \[ t(t-3)(t+3) = 0 \] Since the time \(t \geq 0\), the possible values for \(t\) are \(t = 0\) and \(t = 3\). The problem states the particle starts at the origin, which corresponds to \(t=0\) (since \(x(0)=0^2-6(0)=0\) and \(y(0)=0^3-9(0)=0\)). We are looking for a time \(t > 0\) when the particle returns to the x-axis. This occurs at \(t=3\). Now, we find the x-coordinate at \(t = 3\) using the equation \(x(t) = t^2 - 6t\): \[ x(3) = (3)^2 - 6(3) = 9 - 18 = -9 \] Thus, the particle returns to the x-axis at time \(t=3\) at the x-coordinate -9. This corresponds to choice A.

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Egyptian Scholastic Test (EST I — Literacy & Math)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: Solve the linear system \(3x + 2y = 16\) and \(x - y = 2\) for \(x\) and \(y\).
question.ar: حل the linear system \(3x + 2y = 16\) and \(x - y = 2\) for \(x\) and \(y\).

solution.en:
Step 1: From the second equation, isolate \(x\): \[ x = y + 2 \]

Step 2: Substitute into the first equation: \[ 3(y + 2) + 2y = 16 \implies 3y + 6 + 2y = 16 \implies 5y + 6 = 16 \implies 5y = 10 \implies \mathbf{y = 2} \]

Step 3: Substitute back to find \(x\): \[ x = 2 + 2 = \mathbf{4} \]

The unique solution is \(\mathbf{(4, 2)}\).
solution.ar:

The unique solution is \(\mathbf{(4, 2)}\).

question.en: A school theater sold 250 tickets for a play, raising a total of \(1,750. Adult tickets cost \)9 each and student tickets cost $5 each. How many adult tickets were sold?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Heart of Algebra): A school theater sold 250 tickets for a play, raising a total of \(1,750. Adult tickets cost \)9 each and student tickets cost $5 each. How many adult tickets were sold?

solution.en:
Set up system of equations: Let \(a\) be the number of adult tickets and \(s\) be student tickets: \[ \begin{cases} a + s = 250 \\ 9a + 5s = 1750 \end{cases} \]

Elimination method: Multiply the first equation by 5: \[ 5a + 5s = 1250. \] Subtract from the second equation: \[ (9a + 5s) - (5a + 5s) = 1750 - 1250 \implies 4a = 500 \implies \mathbf{a = 125}. \]

Exactly 125 adult tickets were sold (and \(s = 250 - 125 = 125\) student tickets).

question.en: For what value of the constant \(a\) will the system of equations \(ax + 4y = 7\) and \(3x + 2y = 5\) have no solution?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Heart of Algebra): For what value of the constant \(a\) will the system of equations \(ax + 4y = 7\) and \(3x + 2y = 5\) have no solution?

solution.en:
Step 1: A linear system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct (slopes are equal, \(y\)-intercepts differ). In standard form, this requires: \[ \frac{a}{3} = \frac{4}{2} eq \frac{7}{5} \]

Step 2: Solve the slope equality: \[ \frac{a}{3} = 2 \implies a = 2 \times 3 = \mathbf{6} \]

Check: When \(a = 6\), the ratio of coefficients is \(\frac{6}{3} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\), while the constant ratio is \(\frac{7}{5} = 1.4 eq 2\). Therefore, the lines are strictly parallel with no solution.
solution.ar:

Step 2: حل the slope equality: \[ \frac{a}{3} = 2 \implies a = 2 \times 3 = \mathbf{6} \]

Check: عندما \(a = 6\), the ratio of coefficients is \(\frac{6}{3} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\), while the constant ratio is \(\frac{7}{5} = 1.4 eq 2\). وبالتالي، the lines are strictly parallel with no solution.

question.en: Find all real solutions to the equation \(|2x - 7| = 3x - 1\).
question.ar: أوجد all real solutions to the equation \(|2x - 7| = 3x - 1\).

solution.en:
Step 1: Split into two cases based on the definition of absolute value:
Case 1: \(2x - 7 = 3x - 1 \implies -7 + 1 = 3x - 2x \implies x = -6\).
Check Case 1: \(|2(-6) - 7| = |-19| = 19\), but the right side is \(3(-6) - 1 = -19\). Since \(19 eq -19\), \(x = -6\) is an extraneous solution.
Case 2: \(2x - 7 = -(3x - 1) = -3x + 1 \implies 2x + 3x = 1 + 7 \implies 5x = 8 \implies x = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6\).
Check Case 2: \(|2(1.6) - 7| = |3.2 - 7| = |-3.8| = 3.8\). Right side: \(3(1.6) - 1 = 4.8 - 1 = 3.8\) (Valid ✓).

The only valid real solution is \(\mathbf{x = \frac{8}{5} = 1.6}\).

question.en: Consider the functions \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = x + 7 \). At what \( x \)-value do the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Heart of Algebra): Consider the functions \( f(x) = 2x + 3 \) and \( g(x) = x + 7 \). At what \( x \)-value do the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect?

hints.en: To find the x-value where the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect, we set the two functions equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \).
hints.ar: To أوجد x-value حيث the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect, we set the two functions equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \).

hints.en: Substituting the given expressions for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \): \( 2x + 3 = x + 7 \) To solve for \( x \), subtract \( x \) from both sides of the equation: \( 2x - x + 3 = x - x + 7 \).
hints.ar: Substituting the given expressions for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \): \( 2x + 3 = x + 7 \) To أوجد قيمة \( x \), subtract \( x \) from both sides of the equation: \( 2x - x + 3 = x - x + 7 \).

hints.en: Therefore, the graphs of \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) intersect at \(x\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the graphs of \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) intersect at \(x\).

solution.en:
To find the x-value where the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect, we set the two functions equal to each other: \( f(x) = g(x) \). 

Substituting the given expressions for \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \): 
\( 2x + 3 = x + 7 \) 

To solve for \( x \), subtract \( x \) from both sides of the equation: 
\( 2x - x + 3 = x - x + 7 \) 

This simplifies to: 
\( x + 3 = 7 \) 

Next, subtract 3 from both sides of the equation: 
\( x + 3 - 3 = 7 - 3 \) 

Which gives the solution: 
\( x = 4 \) 

Therefore, the graphs of \( f(x) \) and \( g(x) \) intersect at \( x = 4 \).
